repeat.intro: You are training to be a campus tour guide. Listen to your supervisor and repeat what she says. Repeat only once.
sentences: Welcome to Westfield University.
Please stay together as a group.
The library is on your left.
Students can study here until midnight.
The dining hall serves breakfast starting at seven.
If you have any questions, feel free to ask me during the tour.
Our next stop is the science center, which opened just two years ago.

repeat.intro: You have a new job at a museum gift shop. Listen to your manager and repeat what he says. Repeat only once.
sentences: Good morning, everyone.
The shop opens at ten.
Please check the shelves before we open.
Members receive a ten percent discount.
All returns must include the original receipt.
If a customer asks about tours, send them to the front desk.
Remember to count the money in the register carefully at the end of your shift.

repeat.intro: You are working as a library assistant. Listen to the head librarian and repeat what she says. Repeat only once.
sentences: Thanks for helping out today.
These books need to be returned.
Put the new magazines on the top shelf.
The printers are next to the computer lab.
Quiet study rooms can be reserved online.
Please remind visitors that food is not allowed upstairs.
Books that have been damaged should be placed in the box behind the desk.

repeat.intro: You have started working at the front desk of a fitness center. Listen to your manager and repeat what he says. Repeat only once.
sentences: Hi, welcome to the gym.
Lockers are in the back.
Please wipe down the machines after use.
Yoga classes start every hour on the hour.
Towels can be picked up at the front desk.
Anyone using the pool must take a shower first.
New members are entitled to a free session with a personal trainer during their first month.

repeat.intro: You are a new teaching assistant in a chemistry lab. Listen to the instructor and repeat what she says. Repeat only once.
sentences: Let's begin the lab.
Put on your safety glasses.
Never eat or drink in the lab.
Chemicals must be labeled clearly.
Report any spills to the instructor immediately.
Wash your hands thoroughly before you leave the room.
Broken glass should never go in the regular trash, but in the special container by the sink.

repeat.intro: You are training at a hotel reception desk. Listen to your supervisor and repeat what he says. Repeat only once.
sentences: Welcome to the Grand Hotel.
Breakfast is served downstairs.
Checkout time is eleven a.m.
Your room is on the fourth floor.
The pool is open until nine in the evening.
If you need extra towels, just call the front desk.
Guests who would like a late checkout should let us know by eight in the morning.

interview.intro: A researcher is studying how students manage their time. You have agreed to take part in a short interview. Please answer the interviewer's questions.
questions: How do you usually plan your week?
Tell me about a time when you had too many deadlines at once. What did you do?
Some people say that being busy all the time is a sign of success. Do you agree?
Should universities make time-management training a required course? Why or why not?

interview.intro: A researcher is studying how technology affects learning. You have agreed to take part in a short interview. Please answer the interviewer's questions.
questions: What technology do you use most when you study?
Describe an app or website that helped you learn something new.
Do you think students today rely too much on technology? Explain.
In the future, will online learning replace traditional classrooms? Why or why not?

interview.intro: A researcher is studying travel habits. You have agreed to take part in a short interview. Please answer the interviewer's questions.
questions: What is the most interesting place you have ever visited?
Do you prefer to plan every detail of a trip or to be spontaneous? Why?
Some people think tourism harms local communities. What is your opinion?
Should governments limit the number of tourists in popular destinations? Explain.

interview.intro: A researcher is studying attitudes toward work and careers. You have agreed to take part in a short interview. Please answer the interviewer's questions.
questions: What kind of job would you like to have in ten years?
Tell me about a time when you worked as part of a team. What was your role?
Is a high salary the most important factor when choosing a job? Why or why not?
Some companies let employees work from home permanently. Is this a good idea for companies?

interview.intro: A researcher is studying attitudes toward the environment. You have agreed to take part in a short interview. Please answer the interviewer's questions.
questions: What do you personally do to protect the environment?
Describe a change in your hometown that has affected the environment.
Who should be most responsible for protecting the environment: individuals, companies, or governments?
Would you support higher taxes on air travel to reduce pollution? Explain.

interview.topic: how people spend their free time
interview.intro: A researcher is studying how people spend their free time. You have agreed to take part in a short interview. Please answer the interviewer's questions.
questions: What do you usually do in your free time?
Tell me about a skill you learned outside of school.
Do people today have less free time than people in the past? Why?
Should schools give students less homework so they have more time for hobbies? Explain.

interview.intro: A researcher is studying health habits. You have agreed to take part in a short interview. Please answer the interviewer's questions.
questions: What do you do to stay healthy?
Describe a habit you changed to improve your health.
Should schools do more to teach healthy eating? Why?
Some people believe governments should tax unhealthy food. What is your view?

interview.intro: A researcher is studying how people communicate. You have agreed to take part in a short interview. Please answer the interviewer's questions.
questions: Do you prefer to text or call your friends? Why?
Tell me about a time when a message caused a misunderstanding.
How has social media changed the way people communicate?
Should children be allowed to have smartphones before the age of twelve? Explain.
